title: How to Set Up a Google Business Profile
excerpt: Set up a Google Business Profile step by step: add or claim it, pick a category, hide a home address, set service areas and get verified.
content:
To set up a Google Business Profile, go to business.google.com/add, click "Add your business to Google", enter your business details and choose one of the verification methods Google offers you. It costs nothing. You can only edit the profile once Google has verified that you run the business, and Google says verification reviews take up to five working days.

This guide walks through each step as Google's own help pages describe them today, with the rules that catch most UK and Irish small businesses out: names with keywords in them, home addresses that should be hidden, and verification codes that stop working.

Is a Google Business Profile free and who can have one?

Yes, Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge. What you need is a Google Account. If you have a company email address, Google says you can link it to that account.

Not every business is eligible. Google's guidelines allow a profile for a business that either has a physical location customers can visit or travels to customers where they are. That covers shops, salons, clinics and offices, and it also covers plumbers, electricians, cleaners and other trades who work at the customer's address. It does not cover:

  • Virtual offices: a rented mailing address where the business does not actually operate is not eligible.
  • Businesses with no location customers can visit and that do not travel to customers, such as online only businesses.
  • Co-working desks, unless the office has clear signage, receives customers there during business hours and is staffed by your own staff in those hours.

Google also allows only one profile per business, and one page per location across all accounts.

Should you create a new profile or claim an existing one?

Check first. Your business may already be on Google Maps even if you never added it. Creating a second one gives you a duplicate, which is harder to fix later than claiming the original.

Search Google for your business name and your town, for example "Smith Plumbing Leeds", and look on Google Maps too.

  • If no listing appears, create a new profile (the next section).
  • If a listing appears and nobody has verified it, claim it.
  • If someone else has already verified it, for example a former web designer or a previous manager, Google lets you request ownership from the current owner as long as you are authorised to manage the business.

How to claim a listing that already exists

  1. On a computer, search for your business name and town in Google Maps, or find it on the map.
  2. Click "Claim this business", then "Manage now". In Google Search the link is called "Own this business?", followed by "Manage now".
  3. If Google shows the wrong business, click "I own or manage another business".
  4. Choose a verification option and follow the on-screen instructions.

In the Google Maps app, open the listing, tap "About", then "Claim this business" and "Manage now".

How do you set up a Google Business Profile step by step?

Step 1: Start at business.google.com/add

Sign in to the Google Account you want to own the profile, go to business.google.com/add and click "Add your business to Google". On a phone you can also start in the Google Maps app: tap "Contribute", then "Add place", then "Is this your business?".

A practical tip: use an account the business will keep. If an employee or a web designer sets the profile up on their personal account, the business depends on that person to get back in.

Step 2: Enter your business name exactly as customers see it

Google wants the name you use in the real world: on your van, sign, website and invoices. Its guidelines say that adding unnecessary information to the name is not permitted and could result in the suspension of your profile. Leave out:

  • keywords and service descriptions ("Smith Plumbing, Emergency Plumber Leeds" should be "Smith Plumbing")
  • locations, taglines, phone numbers, website addresses and opening hours
  • words written in capitals for emphasis
  • "Ltd" or special characters, unless your signage or invoices show them as part of the name

Step 3: Choose the right business category

Google asks you to pick categories that complete the sentence "This business IS a", not "HAS a". Use the fewest, most specific categories that describe your core business, and do not use categories to describe features (attributes) or other businesses inside or near yours. An electrician should choose the electrician category rather than adding every related trade they occasionally do.

Step 4: Decide between an address and a service area

This step matters most for trades. Google separates three kinds of business:

  • Storefront: customers come to you at an address with permanent signage, such as a shop or salon.
  • Service area business: you visit or deliver to customers and do not serve them at your address. Google gives cleaning services and plumbers as examples.
  • Hybrid: you serve customers at your address and also go out to them.

If you do not serve customers at your address, Google says to remove the address from your profile and enter only a service area. A plumber who works from home should not show the home address. Google also says a business without permanent on-site signage is not eligible as a storefront and should be listed as a service area business.

For the address itself, Google wants a precise, real address. PO boxes and mailboxes at remote locations are not accepted, and keywords or links do not belong in the address lines.

Step 5: Set your service areas

Service areas are set by town, postcode or another named area. Google does not let you set a radius around your base. The rules:

  • You can add up to 20 service areas.
  • The overall area should not stretch more than about two hours' driving from where your business is based.
  • Be as specific and accurate as possible.

To change them later, open your profile, choose "Edit profile", then "Location", and select "Edit" next to "Service area". Google says approved service area edits can take up to 48 hours to show.

Step 6: Add a phone number and website you control

Give a phone number or website that connects to this business location. Google prefers a local number to a central helpline, the number must be under your direct control, and premium rate numbers are not acceptable. Do not use a link that redirects people elsewhere, such as a social media page, in place of a real website. If you do not have a website yet, our websites for tradesmen page explains what we build.

Step 7: Choose a verification method

At the end of the setup Google offers one or more verification methods. You cannot pick freely: Google says the methods are determined automatically and cannot be changed, based on things like your type of business, public information, region and opening hours.

How does Google Business Profile verification work?

Until you verify, you cannot edit your business information or interact with customers through the profile. These are the methods Google describes:

Phone or text

Google sends a code to the business phone number by call or SMS, and you enter it on the profile. Automated phone menus (IVR systems) cannot receive the code, so answer the call yourself.

Email

Google sends an email to the address shown on the verification screen. Follow the steps in it.

Video recording

Google's verification page recommends video if your business is eligible. It is recorded and uploaded from a mobile phone through your Business Profile ("Get verified", then "Business video"). The video must be filmed live in one continuous take, unedited, at least 30 seconds long. You cannot record it offline and upload it later.

What to show depends on your business type:

  • Storefront and hybrid: the location (street signs, building numbers or nearby businesses), your business name on a permanent sign that matches the profile name, and something only staff can access, such as the till, kitchen or stockroom.
  • Service area business: where you operate (street signs or landmarks near your base), proof the business exists (tools, equipment, business cards or branded clothing) and proof you manage it, for example opening a branded van, doing part of a job, or showing a business permit, invoice or utility bill in the business name.

Do not show bank, tax or ID numbers, private information or other people's faces. Google's example rejection reasons include a business name that is not visible on the storefront and no surrounding area shown, so plan the route through your shot before you press record.

Live video call

Some businesses are offered a live video call with Google instead. It only runs during your opening hours, and you need to be at the business with a device that supports live video.

Postcard

Where postcards are offered, Google mails a five-digit code to your address. Google says most codes arrive within 14 days and expire after 30 days. Two warnings that save weeks:

  • Do not edit your business name, address or category while you wait, or the code will not work.
  • Do not request a new code. Requesting another one invalidates the first and makes the process longer.

Google never asks you for the code, so never share it with anyone.

How long does verification take?

Google says verification reviews take up to five working days, and occasionally longer. You get a confirmation email once the profile is verified, and you can then add owners and managers. Some businesses are verified instantly, for example by verifying the business website in Google Search Console.

If the "Get verified" button appears again, Google could not complete the verification and you need to verify again or try another listed method. If a video was rejected, a "Review issues" option explains what was missing; record a new video that shows everything from the first one plus the missing items.

What should you do once your profile is verified?

Verification is the start, not the finish. Fill in the parts customers read:

  • Opening hours: your regular customer-facing hours. Google says appointment-only businesses should not list hours.
  • Description: what you do and where. Google's rules forbid links, promotions, prices and sales in the description.
  • Photos: your work, your team, your van or premises.
  • Service areas and categories: check them again now that the profile is live.

Keep the business details on your profile, your website and directories the same. Changing business information can trigger a new verification, so make edits deliberately rather than all at once.

Frequently asked questions

Can I use my home address for a Google Business Profile?

Yes, if that is where your business is based, but if customers do not come to your home you should hide the address and show only a service area. Google's guidelines use a plumber working from home as the example.

Can I register a profile at a virtual office or a mail forwarding address?

No. Google says a virtual office or rented mailing address where the business does not operate is not eligible, and PO boxes are not accepted as addresses.

Why did my video verification fail?

Reasons Google gives as examples are a business name that cannot be seen, no surrounding area shown and no proof that you are authorised to run the business. Open "Review issues" for the exact reason and record again.
